  "summary": "S1 [request fact]: The existing dependency-free Node.js help-desk service, README, src/server.js, PORT-based npm start entry point and bin/ CLI define the repository and runtime scope; discovery verifies them. S2 [request outcome]: Add ticket assignment to this service. S3 [request outcome]: PUT /tickets/:id/assignee accepts a valid agent name or null to assign or unassign; discovery resolves the existing response and error conventions and the name edge cases in Q3–Q4. S4 [request outcome]: Assignment changes are permitted only for open and in-progress tickets; discovery establishes the existing status representation. S5 [request outcome]: Assigning the current agent is a no-op; Q4 records the notification default for unchanged assignments. S6 [request outcome]: Every ticket exposes assignee, with null for unassigned tickets; Q5 establishes storage and existing-ticket handling. S7 [request outcome]: The assigned agent receives an assignment notification; Q1 makes discovery responsible for finding the recipient and delivery mechanism, and a person must decide if none exists. S8 [request outcome]: GET /tickets filters by agent or, for an empty assignee value, unassigned tickets, combined with every other supplied filter; Q4 resolves filter edge cases. S9 [request outcome]: The CLI ticket listing displays each assignee, following existing presentation conventions found in discovery. S10 [request boundary]: Preserve all existing service behaviour and pass existing tests unchanged; discovery establishes the baseline. S11 [request outcome]: Add node:test coverage under test/ and run it alongside existing tests with npm test. [Discovery leads, not verified facts]: README.md, src/server.js, bin/, test/, package metadata, runtime configuration and any existing notification, identity or storage documentation and code; no team, channel, internal site, private repository or owner is named. Store any sensitive locator only in an authorized private store, never in committed KNOWLEDGE/. [Interactive-state questions]: Q1 and Q5 cover actors and runtime identity, shared ticket state across people, devices or sessions, its lifetime and end conditions, visibility and existing runtime facilities; until discovery establishes otherwise, use the service's existing state and access model and assume no additional identity, sharing, retention or privacy feature, which rules out inventing them. [Delivery and visibility]: The request authorizes changes in the named service checkout; the API outcome is usable through its HTTP endpoints and the CLI outcome through the existing listing entry point after delivery. An isolated run's source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return; any outcome in a deployed target exists only after release, and no deployed target is named. [Authority and run boundary]: This unattended stage performs intake only, implements nothing and asks no questionnaire; unresolved person-only decisions remain open without blocking independent discovery. [Prior run]: No earlier run or recovery request is identified."
